note: Installed on claude.ai and Claude Cowork on 2026-09-05, on the third upload round. This is the least-modified of the six candidates: the wrapper directory GitHub itself produces is kept, and bin/ becomes .bin/ by prepending one character. The release job builds this combination and names it claude_ai_cowork_rot_dtd_commander_<version>.zip.

released.reproducible: A Windows machine and the Ubuntu runner produced byte-identical archives from the same commit. That is the payoff of the pure-Node writer and the DOS timestamps taken from `git log -1 --format=%cI`: anyone can rebuild the released asset and get the same hash, so the checksum is a claim a reader can check rather than one they must accept.

surfaceReported.why: last read as 129 on the 7.2.0 upload, when two command names were also skill names and shadowed two commands; the archive renames those skills, so the 9.0.0 upload should report 137 (139 minus the two collisions); unconfirmed until that upload is read

baseline.note: Raised from 131 to 134 on 2026-09-06 for the Graphic and Geometric family; the 8.0.0 archive is to be re-proven on upload. Raised from 134 to 139 on 2026-09-07 for 9.0.0: chain, codebase-generator, sigil, verbs and typography; the 9.0.0 archive is to be re-proven on upload, and surfaceReported stays as last read until it is.

whyABaselineAndNotJustRules: A rule says whether this archive is well formed. A baseline says whether the world still looks the way it looked when a human last proved an upload installs. H12 compares the two and fails on any divergence, so a release that adds a command, a skill, a long description or a name collision turns CI red with the reason named. That failure is the signal to update the table, re-prove an upload, and move the baseline forward. Nothing here is meant to auto-heal: a silent fix would hide the very drift this exists to surface.

closed.question: Does renaming a skill in the archive change how that skill is selected?
closed.answer: No. Selection is by description, and the rename touches the name alone. Measured by diffing each renamed SKILL.md against its source: setup-ralph-loop-dtd differs from setup-ralph-dtd in exactly one line, `name:`. ai-slop-gate-dtd differs in `name:` and in its description, but that second change is the H9 length fix (545 to 493 characters), not the rename, and all six of its `Load when` triggers survive it. Both bodies are byte-identical.

closed.question: Can the released archive be rebuilt independently?
closed.answer: Yes, byte for byte. sha256 1bfd24c730594d0e68657b85011221f54f94fdab12eaa1cec07784c21a17bde3 was produced both by the Ubuntu runner and by a Windows machine from commit 4885df3.

open.question: Does the surface enforce any rule nothing has yet triggered?
open.assumption: None beyond the four measured across three rounds. A poor assumption by construction: every rule so far was learned only by violating it, and no schema is published.

H2 is falsified. It was built to refuse a wrapped archive, and a wrapped archive is what worked. The surface strips a wrapper level for the manifest check exactly as it does for the bin check, so every 'missing manifest' report was really the over-long description making the manifest invalid. One fault reported three times.
